# Ashwood Charter — revision notes

Crafted fixture text. These notes describe the invented charter in the sibling
`primary_text/` folder and are written the way a study guide is written, so the ingest
proof has a genuinely different register to chunk.

## What to remember about the signatory list

Fourteen names, and the order is the argument. The miller stands above the reeve, which
tells you grain outranked administration in Ashwood. A question about "what the source
reveals about power" is usually asking about this list, not about the penalties.

## Market days

Two named days, a third promised after harvest. Treat the market clause as the reason the
charter survived: rights that can be counted are rights that get defended in writing.

## The bridge clause

Shared ownership, shared upkeep, three days of labour a year per household. A useful
example when the question asks about obligations disguised as generosity.

## The penalties

Inconsistent units — shillings in some clauses, labour days in others, with no conversion
rule. The heavier fine for blocking the market road than for striking a neighbour is the
detail worth quoting: it prices the town's income above its tempers.

## The reading-aloud clause

The charter was meant to be heard twice a year in the square. This explains the short
sentences and the repetitions, and it is the strongest evidence about the document's
intended audience.
